facts.about: Suzlon Energy Limited is a wind-first group spanning turbine technology/manufacturing, project development/execution, and renewable-asset O&M. It has installed 22+ GW across 17 countries; key subsidiaries include Suzlon Global Services, SE Forge, and Renom.

flags.text: Profit compounding (+3%/yr) lags sales (+41%/yr) over 3 years — margins under pressure
Operating margin expanded 4 pts in 3 years (14% → 18%)
Only 48% of 5-year profit turned into operating cash
Receivable days stretched from 72 to 137 in 3 years
Latest quarter growth (+26%) well below 3-yr trend (+41%)

business.summary: Suzlon Energy Ltd. operates in the wind energy sector, generating revenue through the sale of wind turbine generator (WTG) equipment, project execution, foundry and forging manufacturing, and operation and maintenance (O&M) services.

segments.name: WTG
segments.note: Sale of WTG equipment, components, land sub-lease, and project execution.

segments.name: Foundry & Forging
segments.note: Manufacturing of forging rings and casting articles.

segments.name: O&M services
segments.note: Operation and maintenance of wind turbine generators.

guidance.statement: Normalized EBITDA margin should be around 16.5% to 17% for FY27.
guidance.quote: Normalized EBITDA margin should be, if I normalize for the non-recurring and also commodity, should be around 16.5% to 17%, excluding non-recurring costs pertaining to Suzlon 2.0, FX commodity and impact of West Asia crisis.

guidance.statement: WTG contribution margins are expected to remain in the 22% to 23% range for FY27.
guidance.quote: WTG contribution margins are expected to remain in that 22%, 23% range for FY27, is the belief and it should get normalized subject to some of these externalities getting normalized.

guidance.statement: Suzlon aims to increase its India market share to 40% by FY31.
guidance.quote: I have given my guidance that by FY31, I want to hit 40%.

guidance.statement: The company is targeting a 25% CAGR.
guidance.quote: We have also given a trajectory of 25% CAGR. If you take that trajectory, I also mentioned about exports.

guidance.statement: Annual installations are expected to cross 10 gigawatts in the near term and reach 15 gigawatts by FY31.
guidance.quote: This momentum sets the stage for a multiyear growth cycle with annual installations expected to cross 10 gigawatts in the near term and reaching 15 gigawatts by FY31.

guidance.statement: We should be able to maintain EBITDA margins between 17% to 18% plus minus 1% to 2%.
guidance.quote: My sense is that this year also, plus minus 1% to 2% from there, we should be able to maintain, also we go out and operating leverage plays out in H2, we will certainly see a better positive change to that.

guidance.statement: Capex is guided to be closer to INR700 crores plus or minus INR100 crores.
guidance.quote: So, capex, we had guided even earlier calls also closer to INR700 crores plus minus, maybe INR100 crores depending on the timing and sometimes permits and local issues.

guidance.statement: EPC share will keep increasing to 50% by FY28.
guidance.quote: We also promised that our EPC order share in our order book, EPC share will keep increasing to 50% by FY '28.

guidance.statement: Industry installations expected to cross 10 gigawatt in the near term and reaching 15 gigawatts in 5 years.
guidance.quote: This momentum sets the stage for a multiyear growth cycle with installations expected to cross 10 gigawatt in the near term and reaching 15 gigawatts in the next 5 years.

guidance.statement: Industry installations expected to be around 8 gigawatt in FY27 and 10 gigawatt in FY28.
guidance.quote: Our numbers would be more or less plus/minus you can give some leeway, 8 gigawatt in '27 and maybe 10 gigawatt in '28.

guidance.statement: We would have a run rate of about INR600-odd plus minus 50 going forward.
guidance.quote: We would have a run rate of about INR600-odd plus minus 50 going forward.

guidance.statement: We are firmly on track to achieve our FY '26 guidance of 60% Y-o-Y growth across key KPIs.
guidance.quote: With strong performance in the first 9 months, we are firmly on track to achieve our FY '26 guidance of 60% Y-o-Y growth across key KPIs.

guidance.statement: Each quarter our closing order book will be larger than the opening order book.
guidance.quote: Each quarter my closing -- our closing order book will be larger than the opening order book.

scorecard.promised: Maintain 17% to 18% for FY27, with potential operating leverage in H2.
scorecard.delivered: Margins fell to 16% in Jun 2026 and 15% in Sep 2026.
scorecard.evidence: Operating margins have declined for two consecutive quarters, dropping from 18% in Mar 2026 to 15% in Sep 2026.

scorecard.promised: Targeting a 25% CAGR over the long-term.
scorecard.delivered: Revenue grew 26% YoY in Sep 2026; 3-year trend is 41%.
scorecard.evidence: Sep 2026 revenue of ₹4,876 cr is up 26% YoY, aligning with the 25% CAGR target despite recent deceleration.

scorecard.promised: Firmly on track to achieve 60% Y-o-Y growth across key KPIs for FY26.
scorecard.delivered: FY26 revenue grew 53.6% to ₹16,732 cr; PAT grew 52.6%.
scorecard.evidence: Revenue grew from ₹10,890 cr to ₹16,732 cr (53.6%), slightly under the 60% target for the full year.

scorecard.promised: Closing order book will be larger than opening order book each quarter.
scorecard.delivered: Order book flat at 6.1 GW in Jun 2026 vs 6.0 GW in Sep 2026.
scorecard.evidence: Management reported 6.1 GW in Q1 FY27 (Jun 2026) and 6 GW in Q2 FY27 (Sep 2026), indicating a slight decline.

scorecard.promised: Guided to be closer to ₹700 crores (±₹100 crores) for FY27.
scorecard.delivered: Capital work in progress stands at ₹123 cr as of Sep 2026.
scorecard.evidence: With only ₹123 cr in CWIP by mid-FY27, a significant ramp-up is needed to hit the ₹600-₹800 cr range.

narrative.scoreline: Management has successfully deleveraged the balance sheet but is struggling to maintain margin guidance and order book growth as execution challenges persist.

narrativeVsNumbers.claim: Margin decline is due to non-recurring opex and commodity volatility.
narrativeVsNumbers.reality: Operating margins dropped from 18% to 15% while revenue growth slowed to 26%.

narrativeVsNumbers.claim: Order intake is not an issue; the primary constraint is project execution.
narrativeVsNumbers.reality: Order book has stagnated at ~6 GW for two quarters while revenue growth decelerated.

narrativeVsNumbers.claim: Higher working capital is due to seasonality and gearing up for H2 volumes.
narrativeVsNumbers.reality: Debtor days have stretched to 137 days, and cash conversion cycle is 117 days.

bull: Revenue grew 53.6% in FY26, showing strong scale-up from ₹10,890 cr to ₹16,732 cr.
Balance sheet is practically debt-free with a Debt/Equity ratio of 0.07x and ₹10,277 cr net worth.
Significant tax shield remains with ₹4,400 cr of cumulative profit potential before cash tax outflows.
bear: Operating margins have compressed for three consecutive quarters, falling from 18% in Mar 2026 to 15% in Sep 2026.
Cash flow conversion is poor, with only 48% of 5-year profits turning into operating cash.
Receivable days have nearly doubled in three years, stretching from 72 to 137 days.
watch: Recovery of 10-20% deferred deliveries from Middle East disruptions in H2 FY27.
First confirmed orders from the repowering segment expected by end of FY27.
Monetization of 1,325 MW developmental rights in Andhra Pradesh.

claims.claim: Margin decline was driven by non-recurring opex, commodity/FX volatility, and customer/scope mix changes.
claims.quote: I mentioned non-recurring opex around 100 bps and commodity. This itself is two percentage points. The customer mix changes also depending on the site availability.

claims.claim: Higher working capital is due to seasonality and building inventory for H2 volume growth.
claims.quote: Our net working capital looks higher primarily due to seasonality and us gearing up for higher volumes in H2.

claims.claim: The current order book of 6 gigawatts provides 18 months of coverage.
claims.quote: The current order backlog provides coverage for 18 months, and healthy order pipeline gives strong confidence and comfort for maintaining the growth momentum.

claims.claim: Geopolitical tensions in the Middle East deferred 10% to 20% of deliveries, expected to be recovered in coming quarters.
claims.quote: These disruptions deferred approximately 10% to 20% of deliveries, which is expected to be recovered in coming quarters.

claims.claim: Order book is 6.1 gigawatts with 60% of new orders coming from the DevCo model.
claims.quote: Order book is a healthy 6.1 gigawatt reaffirming our market leadership. In the first 4 months of FY27, we have already secured ~1 gigawatt of orders and continue to have a strong pipeline.

claims.claim: Suzlon expects to log in confirmed orders from the repowering segment in India before the end of this year.
claims.quote: I think in the next 1 or 2 quarters, I should be able to come out and tell you the pilots and the orders that we already cracked -- but the team is very confident that before we end this year, we would have already logged in confirmed order book from the repowering in India first.

claims.claim: The company expects EPC orders to start closing from June onwards, preventing a downward trend in order book.
claims.quote: Right now, we are in advanced stage, and I think you will significantly start hearing from June itself this quarter, the EPC orders getting closed.

claims.claim: Management believes WTG margins will remain stable and not materially decline in FY27.
claims.quote: WTG margins, I don't think materially can go down.

claims.claim: The company has developmental rights for 2.1 gigawatts in AP, with 1,325 MW monetizing in the next 6 months.
claims.quote: Beyond this 775, we have 1,325 megawatt, which will completely get monetized from June onwards in the next 6 months.

claims.claim: Execution remains a challenge due to land acquisition, ROW issues, and grid connectivity delays.
claims.quote: The challenges are the same. Your ROW and first of all land coming in time because the acquiring each land negotiating with farmers becoming a major issue.

claims.claim: Order intake is not an issue for the company; the primary constraint is project execution.
claims.quote: I still maintain the statement which I have been making Sudhanshu every single quarter: order is not an issue for us. The issue is execution

claims.claim: The 5MW turbine is in the proto stage and will be launched at the appropriate time.
claims.quote: our 5 megawatt turbine is now getting into the proto stage and that will come at appropriate time.

claims.claim: The company has significant carry-forward losses that will shield future profits from cash tax outflows.
claims.quote: Even if we don't recognize anything further up to INR4,400 crores of cumulative profit from now on what we get we will not pay single rupee of tax.

risks.text: Contingent liabilities include various tax demands and legal claims against the Company and its subsidiaries.
Impairment assessment of investments and inter-corporate deposits involves significant management judgment and estimation uncertainty.
Recoverability of trade receivables is subject to significant management judgment regarding expected credit losses.
Recoverability of deferred tax assets depends on future taxable profit forecasts and market conditions.
Implementation of a new IT system created risks regarding data migration and internal financial controls.
